sequence_description: Direct-endpoint attack: attempt to inject authorization parameters via an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none). The authorization endpoint must reject an unsigned request JWT to preserve proof integrity.
description: [LLM-Judge] Authorization endpoint appears to accept an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none), which would violate request-object proof integrity if request objects are expected/enforced.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Authorization endpoint appears to accept an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none), which would violate request-object proof integrity if request objects are expected/enforced.

sequence_description: I4 case_confusion: create two local users differing only by username case ('Admin' vs 'admin') and verify they do not collapse to the same downstream subject after login.
description: [LLM-Judge] Test could not evaluate I4 because the OIDC client was never created (client creation failed), causing all password logins to fail with invalid_client.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Test could not evaluate I4 because the OIDC client was never created (client creation failed), causing all password logins to fail with invalid_client.

sequence_description: I4 case_confusion: create two local users differing only by username case ('Admin' vs 'admin') and verify they do not collapse to the same downstream subject after login.
description: [LLM-Judge] Second user creation with username differing only by case was rejected as a duplicate, indicating usernames are treated case-insensitively (may be intended policy, but it prevents testing case-collision principal binding).

evidence.llm_judge_description: Second user creation with username differing only by case was rejected as a duplicate, indicating usernames are treated case-insensitively (may be intended policy, but it prevents testing case-collision principal binding).

sequence_description: I5: Use an unsigned request object (alg=none) to attempt redirect_uri override to an unregistered URI. Expected: request object must be rejected or redirect_uri must remain bound to registered value.
description: [LLM-Judge] Unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none) was accepted (HTTP 200), which is suspicious because it can enable tampering (e.g., redirect_uri override) unless the broker enforces strict request-object signature policy and/or ignores request-object redirect_uri.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none) was accepted (HTTP 200), which is suspicious because it can enable tampering (e.g., redirect_uri override) unless the broker enforces strict request-object signature policy and/or ignores request-object redirect_uri.
